title: Ministry of Law Committee of Supply debate and vote on a $100 budget cut
what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on the Ministry of Law's budget, including a proposed $100 reduction moved by Mr Vikram Nair, which was put to a vote.
why_it_matters: The debate sets out plans to expand civil legal aid to more households, with the per capita household income threshold rising from $1,050 to $1,650 and the savings threshold from $10,000 to $12,000, targeted for later this year. It also covers reforms to civil judgment enforcement, including new Civil Judgment Enforcement Officers, with a Bill planned later this year. The proposed $100 reduction to the Ministry of Law's budget was put to a vote and the 'Noes' had it.

key_points.point: Mr Vikram Nair moved a reduction of $100 to Head R of the Estimates.
key_points.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
key_points.quote: I move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head R of the Estimates be reduced by $100".

key_points.point: MinLaw will review key legislation this year, including arbitration, corporate insolvency and IP.
key_points.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
key_points.quote: This will include, this year, reforms in arbitration, corporate insolvency and IP.

key_points.point: Civil legal aid means-test will be raised to a per capita household income of $1,650.
key_points.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
key_points.quote: We will raise the means-test criteria to a PCHI of $1,650.

key_points.point: Mr Lucien Wong's term as Attorney-General was renewed for three years in January.
key_points.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
key_points.quote: In January this year, Mr Wong's term was renewed for three years.

key_points.point: The Attorney-General appointment process requires the Prime Minister to consult the Chief Justice and the Chairman of the Public Service Commission before advising the President.
key_points.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
key_points.quote: Article 35 of the Constitution provides that the Prime Minister must first consult the Chief Justice and the Chairman of the Public Service Commission (PSC) before tendering his advice as to the appointment to the President.

key_points.point: MinLaw is organising a legal industry gathering titled "The Next Charter: Shaping Singapore's Legal Future Together" on 6 March.
key_points.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
key_points.quote: MinLaw is organising a gathering of the legal industry later this week, we titled it, "The Next Charter: Shaping Singapore's Legal Future Together" on 6 March.

key_points.point: ASME and WIPO will exchange an MOU to set up the WIPO IP Business Centre @ ASME, the first in ASEAN.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
key_points.quote: the Association of Small and Medium Enterprises (ASME) and the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) will exchange a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) in a few days to set up the WIPO IP Business Centre @ ASME – the first in ASEAN.

key_points.point: MinLaw and IPOS will conduct a public consultation later this year on potential refinements to AI-related IP issues.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
key_points.quote: MinLaw and IPOS will conduct a public consultation later this year on potential refinements.

key_points.point: The Guide for Using GenAI in the Legal Sector will be published in the coming weeks.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
key_points.quote: We will be publishing the Guide in the coming weeks.

key_points.point: The LIFT initiative pilot launched in June 2025 has seven Singapore Law Practices participating.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
key_points.quote: We launched the pilot of the Legal Innovation and Future-Readiness Transformation (LIFT) initiative in June 2025 to support these firms to diagnose technology needs and implement tailored legaltech solutions. To date, seven SLPs have joined the pilot.

key_points.point: The ESG-Legal Secondment Programme pilot began in February with a small initial cohort and will be reviewed later this year.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
key_points.quote: we launched a pilot ESG-Legal Secondment Programme this year. MinLaw co-funds secondments for lawyers into participating corporations, giving secondees exposure to ESG business contexts. The pilot began in February with a small initial cohort and we will review its outcome later this year.

key_points.point: SLA transformed state properties at Kampong Java Road into "Flock", an artist-led innovation and creation hub.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
key_points.quote: SLA collaborated with the National Arts Council (NAC) to transform state properties at Kampong Java Road, into "Flock" – an artist-led innovation and creation hub.

key_points.point: SLA worked with Sport Singapore to transform the Gali Batu Flyover area into ARK Sports Village @ Segar.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
key_points.quote: worked with Sport Singapore to transform the Gali Batu Flyover area into ARK Sports Village @ Segar.

key_points.point: SLA launched the sale of the Adam Park heritage bungalow cluster on a 30-year lease.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
key_points.quote: SLA recently launched the sale of the Adam Park heritage bungalow cluster on a 30-year lease.

key_points.point: MinLaw aims to introduce a Bill on civil judgment enforcement later this year.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
key_points.quote: We have been consulting with relevant stakeholders, including the Bar and the Judiciary, and aim to introduce a Bill later this year.

key_points.point: New Civil Judgment Enforcement Officers will be created to assist parties with enforcing civil judgments.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
key_points.quote: creating new Civil Judgment Enforcement Officers to assist parties with enforcing their civil judgments.

key_points.point: The Maintenance Enforcement Division has referred around 1,000 cases since January last year, with about two thirds of concluded cases settled during or after conciliation.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
key_points.quote: Since establishing the new Maintenance Enforcement Division in January last year, the Family Justice Courts have referred around 1,000 cases to the new Division. So far, about two thirds of concluded cases settled during or after conciliation.

key_points.point: The PCHI threshold for civil legal aid will be raised from $1,050 to $1,650, potentially benefiting up to 1,000 more Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents annually.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
key_points.quote: We will raise the PCHI threshold for civil legal aid from $1,050 to $1,650. This could potentially benefit up to 1,000 more Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents annually.

key_points.point: The bank savings and non-Central Provident Fund investment threshold for civil legal aid and criminal defence aid will be raised from $10,000 to $12,000.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
key_points.quote: the bank savings and non-Central Provident Fund investment threshold for both civil legal aid and criminal defence aid will be raised from $10,000 to $12,000

key_points.point: The legal aid expansion is targeted to be implemented later this year.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
key_points.quote: We target to implement this later this year.

key_points.point: The Inclusive Justice Taskforce was launched in January this year.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
key_points.quote: MinLaw formally announced the launch of the Inclusive Justice Taskforce (IJT) in January this year.

key_points.point: The Public Defender's Office has grown to 22 full-time public defender officers.
key_points.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
key_points.quote: We now have grown the PDO with 22 public defender officers, and they are full-time, they are very professional and dedicated.

key_points.point: The Minister declined to say whether there was a long list or shortlist for the Attorney-General appointment.
key_points.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
key_points.quote: I am not going to go into whether there is a long list or a shortlist

key_points.point: The Minister said no individual is indispensable for the Attorney-General role.
key_points.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
key_points.quote: it is not that any individual is indispensable.

key_points.point: The threshold for issuing a mediation direction in community disputes is low.
key_points.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
key_points.quote: the threshold for issuing a mediation direction is low.

key_points.point: The Government is studying the Tampines pilot for the Community Relations Unit and considering expansion.
key_points.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
key_points.quote: We are studying the pilot that is being conducted at Tampines, learning from the experiences, understanding the processes and streamlining it, and in some cases, finetuning it.

key_points.point: IPOS will study IP financing carefully and make announcements in due course.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
key_points.quote: we will study this very carefully and make the announcements in due course.

key_points.point: The amendment to reduce Head R by $100 was put to a vote and the "Noes" had it.
key_points.speaker: The Chairman
key_points.quote: I think the "Noes" have it, the "Noes" have it.

what_happens_next: The proposed $100 reduction was put to a vote and the "Noes" had it, so the reduction was not agreed. The Ministry will proceed with the plans announced, including the civil legal aid expansion targeted for later this year and a Bill on civil judgment enforcement later this year.
